decisions.decision: V2-072 is stage 3, the last stage, of the Repository outcome, and it delivers exactly three things: (1) two bounded records -- a publication intent carried as the outbox Payload and a publication Observation keyed by the operation identifier -- plus the application command that creates the Operation Intent and the Outbox Item in one domain transaction; (2) the first production EffectSink and EffectObserver in this repository, an adapter that turns one verified local commit into one branch on the real forge and then reads that branch back; (3) exactly one live, owner-designated forge write. It deliberately delivers no Pull Request, no HTTP or console surface, no long-running dispatcher loop and no Requirement state change.
decisions.rationale: The task-state outcome asks that an Increment's result 'leaves the machine in a form a person can read', and its three non_goals forbid an unregistered target, forbid treating the push as Requirement completion, and forbid recording a credential value or a raw forge response. A branch on the forge is the smallest artefact that satisfies the outcome: docs/policies/README.md, docs/architecture/overview.md, docs/principles.md and docs/architecture/definition.md each independently state that a Pull Request is not required. Everything else that could be added here (a PR, an owner console panel, a scheduler that calls Dispatch) is a separate surface with its own review, and adding any of them would put the one hard part of this task -- the external side-effect protocol -- behind four other diffs.

decisions.decision: The forge write goes through the forge CLI's Git Data API as a child process (create blob, create tree, create commit, create ref), never through `git push`. `gh auth token`, `gh auth setup-git` and any `credential.helper` configuration are all rejected.
decisions.rationale: This is the decision that makes every other constraint hold without being weakened. Measured on this machine: gh 2.92.0 has a hidden `gh auth git-credential` subcommand (it answers 'accepts 1 arg(s), received 0'), so a credential-helper route technically exists -- and it is refused anyway, because taking it would require four separate concessions at once: adding push to the fourteen-entry git subcommand allowlist, adding credential.helper to the two-key -c allowlist (user.name, user.email), adding HOME to the git child's environment, which V2-071 proved by absence it does not need, and embedding a shell-escaped absolute path to gh inside a git configuration value, which is a new injection surface. `gh auth token` is worse: it prints the credential value on standard output, which is exactly the value that must never enter this process. The Git Data API route needs none of those: the credential never appears in argv, in the environment or in any file, because the CLI reads its own store, which is the V2-017 d8 and V2-064 posture unchanged -- absolute path, filepath.Base equality, guarded base environment of HOME and PATH only, and an empty granted set.

decisions.decision: There is no namespace-versus-push conflict to resolve, because the confinement is not relaxed by one bit and no push is attempted. V2-071's measured refusal ('remote unpack failed: unable to create temporary object directory') is a property of Git's LOCAL file transport under a read-only mount, not a property of push in general: internal/runner/confinement.go states outright that nothing there confines network access, so an HTTPS push from inside that same namespace would not have been refused by the kernel at all. The guarantee that this Loop cannot write to a remote through Git is therefore the argv allowlist, and only the allowlist; the namespace is the second guarantee for filesystem writes, which is what it actually bounds.
decisions.rationale: Stating this precisely is the point of the decision. If the design had claimed the namespace stops remote writes, it would have recorded a guarantee that does not exist, and the first HTTPS remote would have falsified it silently. The honest reading also removes the pressure to relax anything: the git adapter keeps its fourteen-entry allowlist with push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential and worktree absent, keeps NamespaceConfinement on every writing child, and keeps HOME out of its environment. The forge child is a different adapter with a different job: it writes nothing into the Execution workspace, so a mount namespace would bound nothing it does; it is bounded instead by a closed argv shape, an empty granted set, a bounded output cap and a context deadline. The cost, named rather than hidden: the forge child is not filesystem-confined, so it can reach whatever the invoking uid can reach, including its own configuration store. That is the identical posture V2-064 already accepted for the read path, and it is precisely what makes the credential reachable to the CLI and to nothing else in this process.

decisions.decision: What gets published is derived from the VERIFIED commit in the working copy, not from the caller's ChangeSet, and it is read out with the existing fourteen-entry allowlist only: `diff --name-only <base> <head>` for the changed paths, `ls-files --stage -- <path>` for each path's mode and blob object name, and `cat-file blob <object>` for each path's bytes. The allowlist stays exactly fourteen entries. internal/runner/git.go and internal/runner/sourcecontrol.go stay byte-identical; the new methods hang off the same GitSourceControl type from a new file, internal/runner/publishsource.go, behind a narrow second port.
decisions.rationale: A caller's ChangeSet is what it intended; the committed tree is what VerifyIntegrity actually measured. Publishing the former would mean the reviewable artefact was never the verified one. Deriving it needs no new subcommand -- diff, ls-files and cat-file are already allowlisted -- so the strongest property V2-071 established, that no push argv is constructible because the allowlist itself refuses it, survives untouched and can be re-asserted as a regression lock. Keeping git.go and sourcecontrol.go byte-identical also keeps their doc comments true and keeps TestSourceControlHasExactlyOneProductionImplementation and the seven-method port shape unaffected.

decisions.decision: Read-after-write is content-addressed, in four independent equalities. (1) Each blob object name the forge returns must equal the local object name read from `ls-files --stage`. (2) The created tree's object name must equal the local head tree from IntegrityObservation.TreeName, achieved by sending base_tree as the base commit's tree and only the changed entries. (3) After the ref exists, GET the ref and GET its commit: that commit's tree object name must equal the same local head tree, and its parent list must be exactly the one base commit. (4) The ref name must be exactly the ref this operation intended. Only all four together confirm. The local commit's own object name and the published commit's object name are RECORDED and compared as a measurement, never required to be equal.
decisions.rationale: Git object names are content addresses computed the same way on both sides, so blob and tree equality is an exact statement that the reviewer will see the bytes that were verified locally -- which is a stronger claim than a push gives, because a push proves transmission rather than agreement. Commit object names are a different matter: the forge constructs the commit object, and any difference in how author or committer fields are serialised changes its name, so requiring equality would be asserting an unmeasured fact about another system's encoding. Measuring it and recording the result is the honest form, and it costs nothing.

decisions.decision: The observable step is create-only: the ref is created and never updated and never forced. The string 'force' must not appear as a key in any request body this adapter constructs, which a test asserts over every constructed body. The external expected version is therefore the state 'the ref is absent'. If the ref already exists and its commit's tree equals the intended tree, the operation converges as already-successful; if it exists and does not match, the operation is undecidable and goes to needs-input.
decisions.rationale: domain-model.md section 9 step 4 asks for a conditional or idempotent API. Ref creation is exactly the conditional form the forge offers: creating a ref that exists fails, which is a compare-and-set against absence, and it needs no separate idempotency key. A fast-forward update with force=false would also be a compare-and-set, but it widens the operation from 'produce a new reviewable branch' to 'move a branch a human may be reading', so it is excluded. Force is excluded absolutely: there is no state of this Loop in which overwriting a ref a person may have reviewed is the right answer, and the only way to make that a property rather than a promise is that no code path can name the key.

decisions.decision: Only added and modified files with mode 100644 or 100755 are representable. A path whose staged mode is anything else (a symlink at 120000, a submodule gitlink at 160000) and any change that would require deleting a path are refused before any forge call, with a named sentinel. A publication whose changed-path count is zero is likewise refused.
decisions.rationale: V2-071's ChangeFile carries whole content and has no delete form, so a deletion cannot arise from the port as it stands, and a gitlink or a symlink entry cannot be expressed as a blob upload. Refusing them explicitly, before any write, is what stops the adapter from publishing a tree that quietly differs from the verified one. The tree-equality check of d5 would catch such a case afterwards, but only after objects had already been created on the forge, which is exactly the irreversible residue this design is trying not to produce.

decisions.decision: Reads decide the outcome; error text and status codes never do. The adapter parses no HTTP status, discards the child's standard error outright, bounds standard output with a hard byte cap, and returns sentinels whose messages carry none of the child's bytes. Duplicate detection is a GET of the ref, performed before the create as step 2 of the protocol and again after any failure as the read-after-write.
decisions.rationale: This is what makes non_goal 3 ('do not record a raw forge response') structural rather than a review habit, and it follows internal/runner/forge.go, which already discards stderr for exactly the reason that a forge error body can carry a repository name, a scope list or a rate-limit header. It also removes the need to interpret another system's error vocabulary: absence, agreement and disagreement are three states a read can distinguish, and they are the only three the protocol needs.

decisions.decision: The six elements of docs/architecture/domain-model.md section 9 map onto this write as follows, and the existing machinery supplies five of them unchanged. operation_id: minted by the application command through domain.NewOperationID and reused verbatim as the delivery's IdempotencyKey, one per publication attempt of one Execution's commit. Target: the registered Repository's identifier together with the full ref name. Expected version: two distinct notions, both recorded -- the domain Version of the Execution in the Outbox Item, and the external expected state 'ref absent'. Fencing token: minted into the item by the existing Service.effectOutbox, revalidated by OutboxDispatcher.beforeEffect immediately before delivery, and revalidated once more by the adapter's own pre-write re-read of the publication target. Outbox: the existing effectOutbox path with a new outbox kind, so the Operation Intent and the Outbox Item are created in the same domain transaction as the event. Read-after-write: the GET of the ref and its commit described in d5, wired as the existing DispatcherConfig.Observer. needs-input: ObservationUnknown, which OutboxDispatcher.resolveObservation already turns into OutboxNeedsInput.
decisions.rationale: The protocol is already implemented in internal/application/outbox.go -- claim, beforeEffect fence revalidation, deliver outside the transaction, ambiguous, Observe, confirmed/pending/needs-input -- and it has never had a production sink. Writing a fifth implementation of the protocol beside it would be the mistake here. The one thing the existing machinery does not supply is a first-class way for an adapter to say 'I cannot decide', which d10 addresses.

decisions.decision: internal/application/outbox.go receives exactly one addition: an exported sentinel for an undecidable external outcome, and isAmbiguous recognises it alongside the deadline, cancellation and net.Error cases it already recognises. No other behaviour in that file changes and every existing outbox test keeps passing unmodified.
decisions.rationale: needs-input is reachable today only through the ambiguous state, and the ambiguous state is reachable today only by inferring ambiguity from the SHAPE of a transport error. A publication that finds a conflicting ref is undecidable for a reason that has nothing to do with the network, and the only ways to express it without this addition are to wrap context.DeadlineExceeded, which would be a lie about what happened, or to build a second needs-input route beside the protocol, which would defeat the point of the task. One sentinel plus one clause in one predicate lets the adapter state the fact it actually knows.

decisions.decision: Two bounded records live in internal/domain/repository.go, beside the Repository aggregate and the RepositoryObservation and RequirementRepositoryLink precedents it already holds: a publication intent (repository identifier, locator, ref, base branch, base commit, head commit, head tree, changed-path count) which is serialised as the Outbox Item's Payload, and a publication Observation (operation identifier, repository identifier, ref, published commit, published tree, local commit, local tree, a tree-agreement flag, a closed state, a reason, observed_at) which is write-once per operation identifier. Neither record stores a URL.
decisions.rationale: RepositoryObservation established both the shape and the location: forge state enters the Loop as a bounded Observation carrying parsed fields only, in its own keyed record rather than as a field on an aggregate, because a slice on Repository would grow without bound and would turn every publication into a write to one shared document. Keying the Observation on the operation identifier rather than on the Increment is what makes the join to the Outbox Item exact and what makes write-once meaningful under retry: the same operation retried is the same key. No URL is stored because dp-v2-064 d2 already ruled that a URL is never identity and that some URL forms can carry a credential; the human-readable link is derived from the locator, the ref and the commit at the moment it is displayed or written into evidence.

decisions.decision: The publish target is derived only from a registered Repository: the application command reads the Increment, its Requirement, that Requirement's RequirementRepositoryLink and the Repository that link names, all inside the one transaction, and takes owner and name from the stored SourceLocator. A Requirement with no link, a Repository that does not exist, and a Repository whose status is retired are each refused, and no Outbox Item is created. The adapter then re-reads the same target through the application layer immediately before its first write and refuses if it disagrees with the payload it was handed.
decisions.rationale: This is non_goal 1 ('do not push to a repository the owner did not register') made unrepresentable rather than forbidden: there is no field on the request, and no environment variable in production, through which a caller can name a coordinate. Registration is the only way a SourceLocator enters the store, and V2-064 already proved that path. The adapter's own re-read is the section 10 handoff rule -- the next Runner does not trust the Work Packet and re-observes external state -- applied to the one packet that would otherwise be trusted blindly, and it is the same discipline beforeEffect already applies to the canonical control target.

decisions.decision: Branch namespace and reversibility. Every published ref is refs/heads/agentic-loop/<increment_id>/<execution_id>: one reserved first segment, and a name that is a deterministic function of the operation's own identifiers, so retrying one operation targets one ref and a second Execution gets its own. Measured on this repository: the only two push-triggered workflows filter branches [v2] and [main] respectively, so a ref under the reserved prefix triggers no workflow, and the live leg additionally MEASURES this after the write by reading the workflow-run count for the branch and requiring zero. Reversibility verdict: the ref is reversible -- one explicit owner-run delete of the ref removes the reviewable artefact completely -- but two residues are not reversible and are stated rather than glossed: the blob, tree and commit objects created remain reachable by object name after the ref is gone, and the ref-creation entry in the repository's own activity record cannot be deleted at all.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md requires that a capability which cannot be confirmed read-only be exercised reversibly in a dedicated sandbox Repository, and being honest about 'reversible' is the whole value of the requirement. A deletable ref plus undeletable objects plus an undeletable activity entry is what 'reversible' actually amounts to on this forge, and a design that claimed full reversibility would be recording an unmeasured fact. The reserved prefix carries the rest of the safety: it is what keeps the write out of the release-bearing branches, and measuring the workflow-run count converts 'no CI is triggered' from an argument about YAML into an observation.

decisions.decision: The live target is designated by the owner and never defaulted. The live leg is gated on a forge-write gate variable set to 1 together with an owner-supplied <owner>/<name>; with the gate set and the designation absent the check FAILS naming the missing designation, and with the gate unset it skips and is recorded as skipped with its reason, never as a pass. There is no hardcoded default and in particular no default to the Loop's own registered repository. If the owner designates nothing, V2-072 does not fabricate a target: the task goes to blocked with block_reason 'external-unavailable: an owner-designated forge repository that may receive a reversible agent-written branch; needs: designate <owner>/<name> for the forge-write gate, or create a dedicated sandbox repository' and next_owner sol. Creating a new repository, for example a dedicated sandbox, is an OWNER action and this packet does not perform it.
decisions.rationale: V2-071 already established this exact shape for the clone URL and gave the reason: hardcoding a target makes a check's meaning depend on an unmeasured fact about that target. For a WRITE the argument is stronger, because the unmeasured fact would be 'the owner accepts agent-written refs here'. The owner has exactly one repository today and it is the Loop's own release-bearing repository; that repository is admissible under the reserved prefix by d13, but whether it is acceptable is the owner's judgement and not this design's to assume. docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 7 already defines the state to sit in while that judgement is pending, and section 7 also forbids substituting a local or faked result for it.

decisions.decision: The split between make check and live. Inside make check, with no network and no gh child: every constructed argv and request body, every refusal (non-absolute executable, wrong basename, non-empty granted set, invalid owner or name segment, a ref outside the reserved prefix, an unrepresentable mode or deletion, an empty change set, a 'force' key), the derivation of the payload from a REAL local commit made by the real git binary inside the real namespace from a local bare origin, and the whole six-element protocol driven through the REAL OutboxDispatcher and the real memory store against an injected in-process transport that is a function rather than a process. That transport covers four outcomes: ref absent then created, ref already present with the intended tree, ref present with a different tree, and a write whose outcome is unknown. Live, gated: exactly one publication to the owner-designated repository through the real gh child at a resolved absolute path, with the same dispatcher, the same records and a real read-after-write.
decisions.rationale: make check must reach no network, and the parts of this task that can actually be wrong -- the argv, the bodies, the refusals, the state machine, the payload derivation -- are all decidable without one. Faking only the transport, and faking it as an injected function rather than as a fake dispatcher or a fake store, keeps the protocol under test rather than under simulation. What the live leg then adds is the one thing no local test can supply: that the real forge accepts these exact bodies, returns the object names this design predicts, and leaves a branch a person can open.

decisions.decision: Non_goal 2, that a successful push is not a completed Requirement, is guaranteed three ways at once. Structurally: no file this task adds or edits contains a write to a Requirement or an Increment status, which an AST control asserts over the new files rather than a reviewer asserting it by reading. Behaviourally: after a confirmed publication the Requirement's status and version are unchanged, asserted directly. Lexically: the publication Observation's state vocabulary is closed and contains no value meaning completed, resolved or accepted -- its terminal success value means published-and-observed and nothing more.
decisions.rationale: The dangerous failure here is not a wrong line of code but a reader concluding that a green branch means the work is done. Making the conclusion unavailable in the record's own vocabulary is the cheapest durable guard, and cap-autonomous-resolution stays unclaimed for the reason V2-064 recorded and which this task does not change: Preview observation and Stable reflection both depend on a Preview deploy that does not exist yet. contracts/release-contract/** stays byte-identical.

decisions.decision: When the outcome is undecidable the Outbox Item reaches needs-input and the publication Observation records the state and the reason, and V2-072 stops there. It does not move the Requirement to needs-input and does not create a question record for the owner: that surface is V2-065's, and this packet declares the seam instead of building a second one.
decisions.rationale: domain-model.md section 9 says to proceed to needs-input when the outcome cannot be safely decided, and the Outbox Item's own needs-input status plus a recorded reason is the part of that which belongs to the effect. The Requirement-level needs-input question, its reason class, its options and what continues while it waits are exactly the vocabulary V2-065 is chartered to add; duplicating any of it here would produce two ways to ask the owner the same question, which is worse than one deferred connection.

decisions.decision: No production loop calls Dispatch, and that absence is stated rather than left to be discovered. There is no dispatcher construction anywhere outside tests in the tree today: the sink and the observer are wired through the real dispatcher in the deterministic tests and in the live leg, and a scheduled or supervised dispatcher process remains a separate, named follow-on.
decisions.rationale: Writing the first production EffectSink and wiring a long-running dispatcher into cmd are two different changes with two different failure modes, and the second one needs decisions this task has no basis for -- who owns the loop, what its interval is, how it interacts with the Runner's own lease. Naming the gap in the packet is what stops the next reader from taking the silence as an oversight and quietly adding it to some other task's diff.

decisions.decision: Evidence: one record per component this task actually exercises -- domain, application, store-memory, store-firestore, api, runner, docs -- plus one live record under the synthetic component name for the forge write, whose evidence_key is the sha256 of the concatenated constituent component keys with the computation written into the record itself. Every key is read from the final green tree after the evidence is committed. Because V2-045 made the component key the transitive closure of a component's dependency roots, this change moves more keys than it produces records for, so the runner record carries a MEASURED moved-key table -- component, key before, key after -- for every component whose key moved, including the ones this task writes no record for.
decisions.rationale: The manifest states the edges: runner is a declared dependency of api, store-firestore and control-plane, and domain is a dependency of nearly everything, so touching internal/domain/repository.go and internal/runner moves the keys of components this task never edits. Recording a stale key would be recording a value that was true of a tree that no longer exists. Recording the measured table, and letting G6a carry the freshness of everything make check re-runs, is the form that is both honest and finite. The synthetic component name deliberately avoids the provider-live and gcp-live prefixes, because those prefixes trigger the preflight ledger checks in internal/contracts and a forge write has no such approved preflight record.

decisions.decision: V2-072 enters the serialisation chain, and it enters it LAST: V2-071 then V2-069 then V2-067 then V2-073 then V2-068 then V2-065 then V2-072.
decisions.rationale: It has to be in the chain at all because it edits internal/application/ports.go, internal/application/service.go and both store adapters, and every one of the five remaining chain tasks edits at least two of those same files. It has to be last because of G6b: the live exercise is a test in internal/runner, so its compiled file set is the closure reported by `go list -deps -test ./internal/runner`, which includes internal/application -- and every remaining chain task edits internal/application/service.go. Any of them merging after this live observation therefore makes the observation-to-judgement intersection non-empty and forces a re-observation, and a re-observation of this particular exercise is a fresh real branch on a real forge every time. Placing it last makes the cost of the ordering zero instead of one real external write per subsequent merge. The secondary benefit is that V2-065 has landed by then, so the needs-input seam of d17 has something to connect to when someone connects it.

verification: V1. The git subcommand allowlist still has exactly fourteen entries and push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential and worktree are still absent; constructing an argv for each of push, fetch, remote, config and worktree is refused before any process exists. Re-asserted as a regression lock, not assumed.

V2. internal/runner/git.go, internal/runner/sourcecontrol.go, internal/runner/forge.go, internal/runner/confinement.go, internal/runner/supervisor.go and internal/runner/workspace.go are byte-identical at the end; reported with git diff --stat.
V3. The git child's environment still contains no HOME entry, and the forge child's guarded base environment is still exactly HOME and PATH with an empty granted set. Both asserted directly.

V4. The forge executable is resolved to an absolute path whose filepath.Base equals the expected tool name and which stats to a non-directory, all before any process could exist, with an injectable stat hook so every refusal is deterministic.

V5. No credential value appears in any argv, in any environment entry or in any file this adapter writes. Asserted as an absence over every constructed argv and environment, and the words token, secret and credential appear as no field name on any new type in a non-test file.

V6. The publication payload is derived from a real local commit: a bare origin created at test time by the real git binary, cloned into the namespace, changed, verified and committed, then enumerated with diff --name-only, ls-files --stage and cat-file blob. The derived entries' modes and object names equal what the local repository reports.
V7. Every constructed request body is asserted field by field, and no body contains a key named force. The ref creation names the full ref under the reserved prefix.
V8. Four refusals before any write: a ref outside the reserved prefix, a staged mode that is not 100644 or 100755, a change that would require a deletion, and an empty change set.

V9. The four content-addressed equalities of d5 are each asserted, and a deliberate violation of each one -- a blob name that disagrees, a tree name that disagrees, a parent list that disagrees, a ref name that disagrees -- is refused rather than confirmed.

V10. The whole protocol runs through the real OutboxDispatcher and the real memory store, with only the transport injected, across four outcomes: ref absent then created and confirmed; ref already present carrying the intended tree, converging as already-successful with no second create; ref present with a different tree, reaching needs-input; and an unknown outcome reaching ambiguous, then read-after-write, then confirmed or needs-input. The operation identifier and the idempotency key are the same value on every attempt.

V11. The Outbox Item's fence is revalidated before delivery and the adapter's own pre-write target re-read refuses a payload that disagrees with the stored Repository. A stale fence yields superseded and no forge call at all.
V12. A publication request is refused, with no Outbox Item created, when the Requirement has no repository link, when the Repository does not exist, and when the Repository is retired.

V13. The publication Observation is write-once per operation identifier: a second write of the identical Observation is an idempotent replay and a second write with different content is a conflict. Proven identically against both store adapters.
V14. firestore.indexes.json is byte-identical; the per-increment read is a single-field equality query bounded in the storage query in the shape internal/store/firestore/store.go already uses.

V15. Non_goal 2: an AST control asserts the new files contain no Requirement or Increment status write; a behavioural test asserts the Requirement's status and version are unchanged after a confirmed publication; the Observation's state vocabulary contains no completed, resolved or accepted value; contracts/release-contract/** is byte-identical and cap-autonomous-resolution is not claimed.

V16. Non_goal 3: the adapter discards the child's standard error, bounds its standard output, parses no status code, and returns sentinels whose messages carry none of the child's bytes. No record, log, document or evidence summary contains a raw forge response.

V17. make check reaches no network: no test inside it resolves a hostname, opens a socket or starts a gh child. The gh binary is absent from the validated pure PATH, which is measured and recorded rather than assumed.

V18. The single live leg, gated, on the owner-designated repository: the real gh child at a resolved absolute path, one branch under the reserved prefix, the four equalities measured against the real forge, the workflow-run count for that branch measured as zero, and the local-versus-published commit object names recorded as a measurement. With the gate set and the designation absent it fails naming the missing designation; with the gate unset it skips and is recorded as skipped.

V19. G6b: the live record carries its observation commit, and the exercised file set is published as a tracked artifact computed with the same argv V2-075 published, so the observation-to-judgement intersection can be recomputed rather than argued. After the key and the intersection are measured, no file that exercise compiles is edited again in this task.

V20. Determinism: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test; every wait is bounded deadline polling against an injected clock. Every devbox run is judged by its verdict line. Top-level test counts per touched package are reported before and after, and no pre-existing test is renamed, weakened or removed.

V21. Evidence: eight records registered in the index with V2-072 as producer, the ledger tests in internal/contracts green as the definition of done, every key read from the final green tree after the evidence is committed, and the measured moved-key table present in the runner record. gitleaks is run over .agents with the repository configuration before the commit.
risks: R1. The owner may not want an agent-written branch in the Loop's own release-bearing repository, and it is the only registered repository. The design does not decide this for them: the live target is owner-designated, there is no default, and the unresolved state is external-unavailable with next_owner sol. A dedicated sandbox repository is recommended and is an owner action.

R2. The published commit's object name may differ from the local one because the forge constructs the commit object. Mitigated by requiring only the content-addressed blob, tree and parent equalities and recording the commit comparison as a measurement; the risk that remains is a reader mistaking the recorded difference for a defect, which the record's own wording must pre-empt.

R3. Objects created by a failed publication persist on the forge, unreferenced but reachable by object name, and cannot be deleted. Bounded by refusing every unrepresentable case before the first write and by creating the ref only after all objects agree, so the window is narrow; it is not closed, and the residue is stated in the rollback rather than denied.

R4. The forge's Git Data API could reject a body this design predicts will be accepted, which no local test can discover. That is precisely what the live leg exists to find; if it happens the task stops and escalates with the refused step named, and no local result is registered in its place.

R5. Transitive component keys move for components this task never edits, and a stale key recorded anywhere is a false record. Mitigated by measuring the moved-key table and by reading every key from the final green tree after the evidence commit.

R6. The live observation is invalidated by any later change inside the runner test closure, which includes internal/application. This is the M3 gate failure repeating. Mitigated by placing V2-072 last in the serialisation chain and by the completion rule that no file the exercise compiles is edited after the intersection is measured.

R7. Adding a sentinel to internal/application/outbox.go touches the protocol machinery every other effect flows through. Bounded to one exported error and one clause in one predicate, with every existing outbox test required to pass unmodified; if any existing test needs a change, that is the signal to stop rather than to edit the test.

R8. A reader may conclude that a green branch means the Requirement is done. Guarded three ways by d16, and the strongest of the three is lexical: the record cannot say completed because no such value exists in its vocabulary.
